context:
Goal: debts about wrong refusals become notes, as your cull decision says.
Problem (rule): four debts cannot close, because the debt check refuses removing a debt whose Retire line names no test, while the cull decision says a note needs none.
Based on (read): the debt check script reads each removed debt's Retire line for a test name; the cull decision moves wrong-refusal findings to notes with no test.
Departs from: main keeps the four debts open — closes them, either with tests or with a second accepted close path.

options.gain: The debt check keeps one rule for every debt.
options.how: A builder writes one small test per debt so each Retire line names it; the debt check stays as it is.
options.label: Add a test for each (recommended)
options.lose: Four small tests that the cull decision would have skipped.

options.gain: No tests that exist only to close a debt.
options.how: You rule that moving a wrong-refusal debt to the notes file closes it; the debt check learns that second path.
options.label: A move to notes closes it
options.lose: Goes against your ruling: a repo changes to fit a shared tool, never the tool to fit a repo. The debt check gains a second way to close.

reply: Closed 18:53 CST: withdrawn, already settled by your cull ruling of Nov 10 15:04 CST (decision cull-guard-wrong-refusals): after the cull, a wrong refusal is a note only, with no red test. The debt check is brought in line with that ruling.
title: How do four debts about wrong refusals close, when the debt check wants a test and the cull says a note needs none?
why: Two of your rules disagree: the debt check and the cull decision.
